text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is not itself evidence of discrimination. It's common in broadcasting, and panels of men appoint women routinely. On its own it proves nothing — but it is relevant context if other things point the same way, and in some jurisdictions panel composition is a procedural failing worth noting.

Your stronger ground is elsewhere: seven years' more experience, including five as deputy, and a stated reason ("strong experience of digital media") that may or may not have been a published criterion. Check the original job spec. The unanswered two-week-old request is also a concrete failing.

So: chase the written reasons first, citing the spec. Mention the panel as background, not as your headline claim — leading with it invites dismissal.
